questions.prompt: In RestAssured's given/when/then style, what goes in `when()`?
questions.explanation: given() builds the request, when() performs the call, then() verifies the response.

questions.prompt: Which assertion checks that a JSON field `status` equals "open"?
questions.explanation: `.body(path, matcher)` uses a GPath expression and a Hamcrest matcher. `.header` checks HTTP headers, not body fields.

questions.prompt: `.statusCode(201)` inside then() fails the test if the response status is anything other than 201.
questions.explanation: It is an assertion. A different status throws an AssertionError with the actual value.

questions.prompt: The body is `{"items":[{"price":5},{"price":12},{"price":8}]}`. Which assertion passes?
questions.explanation: `items.price` collects [5, 12, 8], which has items 5 and 12. It is a list, not 5; the size is 3; index 3 does not exist (zero-based, the last is items[2]).

questions.prompt: How do you extract the created id to use in a later request?
questions.explanation: `extract().path(...)` returns the value after the assertions run, so the id is only used if creation succeeded.

questions.prompt: Which belong in a shared RequestSpecification built with RequestSpecBuilder? Select all that apply.
options: The expected status of each test
questions.explanation: Request specs hold common request setup. Expected statuses vary per test and belong in then() (or a ResponseSpecification for shared response checks).

questions.prompt: This test fails with: Expected: <19.99> but was: <19.99>. Why?
options: The JSON number is parsed as a Float, while 19.99 in Java is a double; compare with 19.99f or configure JsonConfig to use doubles/BigDecimal
questions.explanation: By default RestAssured maps JSON decimals to Float, and Float(19.99) does not equal Double(19.99). Use `equalTo(19.99f)`, `closeTo`, or `JsonConfig.jsonConfig().numberReturnType(BIG_DECIMAL)`.

questions.prompt: Your suite logs every request and response with `.log().all()` in CI. A reviewer raises a concern. What is it?
options: Logs can expose Authorization headers, tokens and personal data in CI output; log only on failure (`log().ifValidationFails()`) and mask secrets
questions.explanation: CI logs are widely readable and retained. Logging only on failure keeps debugging power while limiting exposure; RestAssured can also blacklist headers from logs.

coding.title: A tiny request builder with checks
coding.prompt:
RestAssured needs a running API, so practise the same ideas in plain Java. Create `OrderRequest` with a fluent builder: `OrderRequest.builder().baseUri(String).path(String).query(String key, String value).build()` and a method `url()` that returns the full URL. Query parameters appear in insertion order, URL-encoded with `URLEncoder.encode(value, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)`. `build()` must throw `IllegalStateException` if `baseUri` is missing.

Example: base `https://api.test`, path `/orders`, query `status=open`, `q=a b` -> `https://api.test/orders?status=open&q=a+b`.
coding.explanation: This is the pattern behind RequestSpecBuilder: fluent setters returning `this`, validation in `build()`, and an immutable result. LinkedHashMap keeps insertion order so URLs are predictable in assertions.
hints: Each builder method sets a field and returns `this`.
Use a LinkedHashMap for query parameters.
coding.runInstructions: Create a Maven project with JUnit Jupiter 5 as a test dependency (Java 17+). Put `OrderRequest.java` in `src/main/java/` and `OrderRequestTest.java` in `src/test/java/`, then run `mvn test`. All three tests should pass.
